source.title: Competency-based education for CBSE — Item Bank: Science Class 9 (September 2021)
source.subject: science
source.authorityName: Central Board of Secondary Education (content created by the British Council)
source.usage: Official CBSE item bank, freely available on cbseacademic.nic.in for teachers to use as they wish; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: A bank of practice items (not an examination paper), 'Competency-based education for CBSE, Item Bank: Science Class 9, September 2021', content created by the British Council. Each item begins with a metadata table (item identity, assessment objectives, content references, marks), then source material, the questions and a mark scheme (Answer / Guidance). Every item's question is numbered '1' in the document, so 'number' holds the printed item identity (e.g. 'Science9MB3') and 'part' the question label inside it. The introduction (which says 'Science Class 8' in error) counts 59 items; item Science9RK31 (satellite in uniform circular motion, pp.56-59) is printed a second time as 'Science9RK3' on pp.96-99 with identical questions and mark scheme; that duplicate copy was not extracted again. Items map to the NCERT books current in 2021; chapters were mapped by topic to the current NCERT 'Exploration' (Grade 9, 2026) chapter list and must be confirmed by an editor. Items on topics without a matching chapter in the current book (crop production and farming, fertilisers and manure, animal husbandry, health and disease, states of matter, density) have chapter null. Where a question's printed marks disagree with the item metadata, the value used is stated in that question's extractionIssues. Introduction, item index, assessment objectives and metadata tables were skipped. Level-of-response tables in the mark scheme are summarised as '(Marked by level of response, levels 0–4.)'.

questions.text: This question is about different methods of farming. The Sahel dry-land zone is located south of the Sahara Desert in Africa. The rainfall is less than 400 millilitres a year. To prevent more land becoming desert, farmers are returning to traditional methods of agriculture. These methods include: • regularly moving herds of cattle, sheep and goats to different fields • planting acacia trees around the edges of fields • placing thorny branches and rocks in the beds of streams • digging pits in the fields during the dry season to fill with organic matter Discuss these methods with reference to: • Overgrazing • Producing compost • Soil erosion • Soil fertility

officialAnswer.text: Indicative Science: • Movement of livestock prevents overgrazing; • Less overgrazing less exposure of soil to wind erosion; • Droppings from livestock adds fertility to soil; • Decay of organic matter in pits adds fertility to soil; • Pits trap rainfall – wet soil less likely to blow away; • Branches and rocks slow down the flow of water; • Slower water has more time to deposit fertile silt; • Compost in pits are idea for germinating seeds; • Organic matter in pits retains moisture for crops; (Marked by level of response, levels 0–4.)
